title: Chapter 29
content:
"Holy shit. No matter how many times I look at it, that thing is fucking massive."

Leaning against the second-floor railing, Kang Seok-joo stared down at the courtyard, his voice caught somewhere between awe and crude disbelief. Below, the estate staff was filling the newly completed basin. The tiles were a vivid cobalt blue, radiating a crisp, cool gleam in the afternoon sun.

Turning on his heel, Seok-joo sauntered over to Jakyeong. He was impeccably dressed in a tailored black suit, his hair neatly slicked back with pomade. He’d hate the comparison, but sharp and put together, the resemblance to Kang Il-hyun was uncanny.

"Hurry up and change. You're coming with me."

Seok-joo was pushing him to attend a funeral. A few days ago, an explosion had leveled one of Choi Ki-tae's processing warehouses, wiping out his younger brother alongside a dozen enforcers. Seok-joo asked if Jakyeong had caught the brief television segment, but Jakyeong merely shook his head.

Despite the body count, the incident had barely made a ripple in the press. The authorities had held the remains under the pretense of an ongoing investigation, finally releasing the bodies for funeral rites today. In reality, the investigation was pure theater—the police were sweeping the whole affair under the rug.

"How the hell does one person pull that off?" Seok-joo scoffed. "Every single guy in there had his head completely blown open."

Jakyeong contorted his face into a picture of squeamish disgust. "That sounds... awful."

"They say it was one-shot, one-kill across the board."

Seok-joo formed a finger gun, aiming it at the ceiling. Bang, bang, bang. Then he swiveled his arm, leveling his index finger between Jakyeong's eyes. Look at that sloppy form, Jakyeong thought dryly. You need to enlist in the military, you little punk.

"Hands up," Seok-joo sneered.

"Cut it out... That's not funny."

Lowering his hand, Seok-joo burst into a fit of giggles. "If it were me, I would've never gone out like a bitch. Imagine getting taken out by a single shooter. Pathetic, isn't it?"

Judging by his sheer excitement, one would think he was heading to an upscale nightclub rather than a memorial service. Then again, Jakyeong already knew the bad blood between Ki-tae and his late brother—the dead kid’s contact name on Ki-tae's phone had literally been saved as Piece of Shit.

"I bet the second the incense burns out, Ki-tae throws a celebratory rager," Seok-joo chuckled.

"His own brother just died."

"I get it, honestly. If Executive Director Kang dropped dead tomorrow, I'd pop champagne."

Seok-joo ground his teeth, the bitterness rolling off him in waves. The scar on his temple had faded considerably since their first meeting. Il-hyun had driven an ice pick into the kid's skull—surviving that level of lethal intent was a miracle in itself.

"Just to be clear..." Seok-joo added, his bravado instantly evaporating into a nervous whisper, "...you're not repeating any of this to my brother, right?"

Talking tough only to immediately check his six was peak Seok-joo.

"Of course not... We're not that close."

"Right? You two have completely different personalities anyway. There's no way you'd hit it off."

Seok-joo puffed out his chest, clearly proud of the delusion that he held more sway over Jakyeong than his brother did. You might think you're closer in spirit, Jakyeong mused silently, but physically, your brother has you beat by a mile. They had already rolled around naked in bed together. Though Jakyeong would rather die than admit he hadn't exactly hated every second of it.

Jakyeong had anticipated a sterile hospital mortuary, but the funeral was hosted at a sprawling Buddhist temple nestled on the outskirts.

Outside the temple gates, sleek black sedans were parked bumper-to-bumper, while hundreds of men in dark formal suits flooded the courtyard. Convoys of luxury vehicles arrived in tight formations, unloading crews of heavy-set men who marched up the stone steps toward the main memorial pavilion.

White chrysanthemum wreaths flanked the pathways, and beneath massive blue tarps pitched in the courtyard, clusters of syndicate guests were already seated around long folding tables, eating and drinking.

Walking beside Seok-joo, several attendees recognized the Chairman's youngest son, stepping forward to exchange respectful bows and inquire after Chairman Kang's health.

As they neared the inner sanctuary, the pungent, heavy aroma of burning incense filled the air. Inside the altar hall, Choi Ki-tae stood near the entrance, wearing the black mourning armband of a chief mourner as he received guests.

Following Seok-joo, Jakyeong slipped off his dress shoes and stepped onto the polished wooden floor. Framed by a sea of white chrysanthemums, the portrait resting on the altar showed the blond youth whose skull Jakyeong had caved in with a bullet just days ago.

Jakyeong lit an incense stick, placed it in the bronze censer, and bowed deeply alongside Seok-joo. May you burn in the deepest pit of hell for eternity, Jakyeong prayed with absolute serenity. The world is a much safer place without garbage like you breathing its air.

"Thanks for making the trip out here," Ki-tae said, stepping forward with an extended hand. His face held not a single trace of grief.

Taking his palm, Jakyeong offered soft condolences. "I'm so sorry for your loss..."

Ki-tae let out a quiet smirk, dropping his voice. "Don't worry about it. It's not a huge loss."

Another absolute bastard.

Before Jakyeong could force a response, a sudden ripple of hushed murmurs swept through the entrance. Turning his head, Jakyeong saw Kang Il-hyun striding through the pavilion doors, with Park Tae-soo trailing close behind.

The atmosphere in the hall shifted instantly. Conversations died down as men scrambled to drop into deep, ninety-degree bows. Guests sitting at the outdoor tables immediately set down their spoons to pay their respects, and even senior syndicate elders inclined their heads as Il-hyun passed.

Even surrounded by hundreds of ruthless underworld figures, Il-hyun’s imposing, lethal presence was unmistakable. It made Chairman Kang's deep-seated wariness of his second son entirely understandable.

Il-hyun wore a genial, polished smile.

Beside Jakyeong, Seok-joo muttered under his breath, "Fucking hell... repulsive even from across the room..."

Ki-tae chimed in with a sneer. "Someone go block him before he comes over here. Looking at that face is gonna make me throw up my spicy beef soup."

A white-haired man wearing the same mourning armband as Ki-tae approached Il-hyun from the inner altar. With his back turned, his face was obscured, but Jakyeong watched the exchange intently. Il-hyun clasped the man's hand, offering words of comfort with a look of profound, solemn sympathy. Incredible acting, Jakyeong noted. You've got me beat in the theater department.

As their conversation wrapped up, Il-hyun began walking toward the front corridor. The white-haired patriarch turned around to greet other mourners—and the moment Jakyeong caught a clear look at his face, his vision locked tight.

It was him.

The man who had supplied narcotics to Jakyeong's biological parents. The man who used to stroll into their dilapidated home to roll around with his mother on the porch. The man who had kicked down their door with a wooden club, screaming that his father had skimmed product.

The man who had ordered ten-year-old Jakyeong butchered.

Fifteen years had dusted his hair with gray, but the predatory curvature of his features remained unmistakable. The man turned back toward the courtyard, moving from table to table to thank the guests.

Seok-joo gave Jakyeong’s elbow a sharp nudge. "Yi-an, let's get out of here."

They were a second too late.

Before they could reach the shoe cubbies, Kang Il-hyun was standing directly in their path. Hands shoved deep into his trouser pockets, Il-hyun tilted his chin up, looking down at the two of them with cold, displeased eyes.

The suffocating pressure of his stare snapped Jakyeong back to the present. He could practically hear Seok-joo’s internal panic spiraling beside him. This was Jakyeong's first excursion since the sniper incident—and he hadn't asked for permission.

"What brings our two young masters all the way out here?"

"Brother... I, uh, I just came to offer Ki-tae some support..."

Il-hyun’s gaze shifted smoothly from Seok-joo to Jakyeong. "And you, Yi-an?"

Jakyeong glanced sideways at Seok-joo. While following the kid had provided the ride, putting a face to the man who ruined his childhood had been his true objective.

"I came... to pay my respects as well."

"To whom?"

Jakyeong turned his head slightly toward Choi Ki-tae, who was occupied receiving another wave of guests near the threshold. "To... Mr. Choi over there."

The temperature in Il-hyun's dark pupils dropped to freezing. "I had no idea you two were so close."

"We're not close..." Jakyeong murmured, casting his eyes downward in meek deference. "I was just taught that when someone experiences a tragedy... it's proper manners to share in their grief."

Il-hyun’s left eyebrow arched into a sharp angle. Looking closer, Jakyeong spotted a faint, fresh laceration resting just above the brow. He vanished from the house for two full days... was he out settling scores?

"Look who it is. Seok-joo, my boy."

Ki-tae's father approached with slow, heavy steps. Up close, the toll of the last few days was written clearly across his face—shadows clung to his hollow cheeks, and deep grief was warring with a bitter, simmering rage in his eyes.

Il-hyun cast one last, unreadable glance at Jakyeong before stepping past them into the main altar hall.

Seizing the opening to slip away, Jakyeong moved toward the exit, but the old patriarch stopped him with a gentle inquiry.

"And who might this young gentleman be...?"

"My name is Jang Yi-an, sir... I'm visiting from Hong Kong."

"Ah, of course. Thank you for making the journey."

The man extended his right hand.

It was the very hand that had groped his mother and backhanded young Jakyeong bloody across the dirt. If circumstances allowed, Jakyeong would have drawn a blade and severed the limb at the wrist without blinking.

Instead, he reached out and took the hand in a respectful, two-handed clasp.

"Please accept my deepest condolences, sir... May your son rest in peace."

The man patted the back of Jakyeong’s hand with soft, weary strokes. "Thank you. Such a thoughtful young man."

Jakyeong kept his gaze respectfully lowered to ensure not a flicker of murderous intent leaked through his irises.

Releasing his grip, the old man paused, studying Jakyeong's face with a faint, quizzical tilt of his head. "Have we... crossed paths before?"

"This is our first meeting, sir."

A faint, tired smile touched the patriarch's lips. "I suppose so. A face as striking as yours isn't one a man forgets easily."

The ruthless, venomous thug from his childhood had withered into nothing more than an aging, broken father mourning a dead son. The old man urged them to grab a hot meal beneath the tent before leaving, then turned and shuffled back toward the altar.

Jakyeong and Seok-joo retrieved their shoes and hurried down the stone steps before Il-hyun could reemerge. Seok-joo leaned in close, whispering under his breath.

"Let's eat somewhere else. That soup's gonna give me an ulcer."

Jakyeong couldn't agree more. But before they could clear the outer gate, a deep, smooth baritone cut through the afternoon breeze behind them.

"Yi-an."

Seok-joo squeezed his eyes shut, mouthing a silent, panicked curse.

They turned around to find Kang Il-hyun descending the stone steps toward them.

"If you're heading home, ride in my car."

His tone was polished and polite, but the authority behind it was absolute.

Jakyeong hesitated, gesturing toward Seok-joo. "I was planning to ride back with Seok-joo..."

Il-hyun’s gaze drifted over, locking onto his younger brother like a laser sight. "Is that so?"

Predictably, Seok-joo was already backpedaling down the gravel path. Stammering that an urgent prior engagement had just slipped his mind, the kid dropped into a frantic ninety-degree bow to avoid catching Il-hyun's wrath, then turned and bolted toward the parking lot.

Jakyeong let out a quiet, resigned sigh through his teeth. Cowardly little shit.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Mourning Armbands (상주 완장): In Korean funeral customs, chief mourners (the primary male relatives responsible for the funeral rites) wear white armbands with two black stripes on their left sleeve, indicating their direct familial duty.

  • Funeral Beef Soup (육개장 - Yukgaejang): Traditional spicy shredded beef soup with scallions and chili oil is the standard dish served to guests under the dining tents at Korean funerals. The red color was historically believed to ward off evil spirits and negative energy.

  • Buddhist Temple Funerals (사찰 장례식): High-ranking underworld figures or traditional families in South Korea often hold elaborate, multi-day Buddhist memorial services at secluded temples to accommodate large crowds, ritual chants, and discrete security perimeters away from the public eye.
